messages.subject: Key rotation status + the notification question
messages.body:
Marta,

Rotation status: 4 of 6 internal keys done overnight, customer integration tokens running now under the 24-hour dual-validity window, done by tonight. No broken syncs so far.

The open item is customer notification. Ravi's timeline doc confirms the exposed fork was public for ~3 weeks. The staging key could not read customer data directly, but the token inventory shows 9 customer integrations whose credentials share the exposed prefix and must be treated as potentially compromised. My take: those 9 need to hear from us regardless of what the lawyers say — I would rather they hear it from us than from a security blogger.

Can you and Helen make the call on whether and when we notify? If yes, Aisha drafts, I supply the technical wording.

Cheers,
Dev
Dev Raman | CTO | Parcelwise B.V.

messages.subject: RE: Key rotation status + the notification question
messages.body:
Dear Ms Kowalczyk,

Further to Mr Raman's summary, our advice is as follows.

Where personal data may have been accessible through the exposed credentials, a data-protection notification duty is engaged. Notification to the relevant supervisory authority and to the affected data subjects is required without undue delay and, in any event, within 72 hours of the controller becoming aware of the incident, where feasible. On the facts described, awareness dates from 3 March; notification should therefore be completed by 6 March 2026.

We recommend notifying the nine affected customers regardless of whether the technical assessment ultimately confirms data accessibility, as an inability to exclude the risk is itself material. Draft notices should avoid speculation as to cause and should describe the remediation taken.

Yours sincerely,
Nadia Petrova
Okafor Lindqvist Advocaten

messages.subject: RE: Key rotation status + the notification question
messages.body:
then we notify. all 9, by friday. aisha drafts, dev checks the technical wording, nadia sees the final text before it goes. no guessing in the letters — facts and what we fixed.

Sent from my iPhone

messages.subject: RE: Key rotation status + the notification question
messages.body:
Hi team 😊

Understood — draft coming to Dev and Nadia before end of day tomorrow. I will call the two accounts I know best personally first: the owners of both have told me before that they would rather get a phone call than a formal letter on anything scary, and I agree with them. The other seven get the written notice plus a direct contact person (me) for questions.

One ask: can the notice include the exact date the rotation of their token completed? In my experience customers calm down considerably when the letter says "your new credentials were active as of..." rather than "we are investigating".

Aisha

messages.subject: RE: Key rotation status + the notification question
messages.body:
Good ask — yes. I'll send you a per-customer table tonight with: token rotation completed-at timestamp, whether the token was dual-valid (all of them), and one plain-language line on what the exposed credential could and could not access. Use exactly that table in the letters; no adjectives beyond it.

Wording rule for the draft: "we rotated all credentials as a precaution" is accurate, "there is no evidence of misuse" is accurate, "no data was accessed" is NOT — we cannot prove that. Nadia will strike it if you try.

Cheers,
Dev
Dev Raman | CTO | Parcelwise B.V.

messages.subject: RE: Key rotation status + the notification question
messages.body:
Dear Marta,

Confirming the plan is on my record as well: notification to all nine affected customers to be completed by Friday 6 March, per Nadia's advice on the 72-hour duty, with final text cleared by Nadia before sending. I will also log the notification dates for each account in case questions arise later from customers or the authority.

Kind regards,
Helen

Helen Oyelaran | Chief Financial Officer | Parcelwise B.V.
